messages:
Marc: quick alert: cluster dedicated-gpu-3 seeing a cluster of OOMs over the last hour after last night's kernel-selector change. ~1.8% of in-flight requests hit OOMs, mostly long-chat flows.

Anita: can you share the profiler dump / sample request ids?

Marc: uploading a trace (s3 link) and pasting a small excerpt. model=redwood-chat-7b-v2 (int8), selector=fast-fused-pref. Example log: 
```
[2026-03-11T04:11:02Z] req=qqc001 seq=900 batch=1 selected_kernel=fused_attn_fast est_workspace=1.4G kv_live=640M allocate(temp)=320M -> OOM
[2026-03-11T04:11:03Z] allocator: fragmentation_ratio=0.38 cudaMalloc failed
```
Full trace: s3://redwood-perf/allocator/176327/qqc001.trace.pb

Jess: looks like a pattern: fused kernel wins for mid-high seq len, but workspace estimate didn't include dynamic kv resize + incremental temp buffers from token callbacks. allocator fragmentation then prevents a large realloc.

Rui: confirmed on sim run: when auto-batcher accumulates small groups and then a long-seq single request lands, kv cache grows during generate and we exceed the peak window we estimated. Fragmentation makes cudaMalloc fail even if total free bytes marginally sufficient.

Olga: are most OOMs on single-host (no model sharding)?

Marc: yes single-host. Batching window is 30ms auto-batcher. Also noticed many streams with persistent KV across conversation history, pushing per-conversation kv beyond defaults.

Jess: immediate mitigations we can flip from runtime flags:
- runtime.buffer_reuse=true (force temp buffer reuse pool)
- allocator.guard_alloc=true (try best-effort compaction before falling back)
- kernel_selector.memory_threshold=0.75 (prefer memory-saver kernel when estimated usage > 75% of available)
- max_kv_per_request=600M (soft cap + eviction policy)
- reduce batching.window_ms=8 (shorter window reduces peak aggregation)

Anita: can we implement an ingress-level request-shaper: reject or throttle very long sequences with 429 or partial-response opt-in? Would like to avoid user-visible errors but need to reduce blast radius.

Marc: rolled a lightweight Envoy Lua filter to apply sequence-length routing: seq>1200 -> route to slow-pool or return 429 if slow-pool saturated. Deployed to dedicated-gpu-3 5m ago.

ci-bot: rollout ci/runtime/allocator-pool@sha2beef started (10% -> 100%)

Leo: what's inside allocator-pool?

Jess: two changes: 1) pre-allocated slab pools for small temps (<=64KB, 64KB-1MB, >1MB) to avoid repeated cudaMalloc; 2) a conservative workspace cap per-layer computed as min(heuristic, global_budget - current_kv - reserved_headroom). Also an on-alloc fallback that checks total projected peak (workspace + kv + temps) and flips kernel choice if > threshold.

Rui: we also added an eviction hook: when kv_current > kv_soft_limit, evict oldest segments for convs idle > kv_idle_threshold. This reclaimed ~150-300MB per active conv in our tests.

Olga: any observed latency regressions with the memory-saver kernel?

Marc: so far p50 unaffected, p95 for long seqers increased ~8-15% when fallback triggers. OOMs dropped from 1.8%->0.15% in last 20m after flags + routing.

Jess: propose a concise OOM runbook entry (for oncall):
1) detect: alert if OOM_count > 5 in 5m OR allocator_fragmentation > 0.3 AND OOM_rate trending up
2) quick mitigation (automated play): enable runtime.buffer_reuse, set kernel_selector.memory_threshold=0.7, set batching.window_ms=10
3) secondary: route seq>1024 to slow-pool; enforce max_kv_per_request=512M with on-demand eviction
4) if still failing: enable circuit-breaker for new long-seq requests with 429 + Retry-After header; at this point page oncall
5) post-incident: collect profiler trace (profiler --trace-workspace --alloc-map), allocator heap dump, KV footprints, and run allocation-fuzz test in staging

Anita: addendum: include a rollback hook in deployment pipeline so a high OOM spike can auto-rollback the last kernel-selector change. We should also tie this to automated canary gating.

Leo: long-term backlog items to add to eng-runtime roadmap:
- unified accounting: a single estimate function that sums kv + workspace + temp buffers with uncertainty bands
- reactive compaction: lightweight defragmentation on GPU during low-util windows (similar to OS buddy compaction idea)
- smarter batching heuristics: early-exit batched groups if an incoming long-seq request would push peak over threshold
- pre-alloc mode for heavy-traffic convs: pre-reserve dedicated workspace to avoid fragmentation impact

Rui: also recommend a KV placement policy: large, cold conversational history moved to SSD-backed paged-kv which can be rehydrated; keep only hot segments in GPU RAM. Reduces steady-state per-conv footprint.

Olga: I'll write a short test in the runtime smoke suite that simulates concurrent small batches + mid-long single sequences to ensure fallback path triggers correctly and returns 200 with slower kernel or 429 depending on config.

Dina: eng-sre: created SR-3289 automating rollback-on-oom spike; will add runbook steps and link to this thread.

Marc: one more operational tweak: add metric histograms for (estimated_workspace, actual_workspace, kv_size) and a derived gauge peak_projection = est_ws + kv_size + temp_peak. We can alarm on peak_projection > 0.8*gpu_total.

Jess: note for rollout policy: block kernel-selection changes unless staging regression <5% alloc increase and staging OOM==0 for 72h. Also store workspace traces per canary for audit.

Marc: thanks all. leaving thread open for 24h post-stability. I'll post the postmortem skeleton once we have 24h without recurrence.

eng-sre-bot: issue SR-3289 created and linked to thread. Assigned to @Dina.

ci-bot: perf traces archived at s3://redwood-perf/allocator/176327/
